main_text.head: Marathon oppidum Atticæ.
main_text.p: Stat. Theb. Lib.12.Si patrium Marathona metu, si tecta leuasti Cresia, nec fudit vanos annus hospita fletus.
Seneca Hip-polytus.Vos, qua Marathon tramite lœuo Saltus aperit, qua comitata Gregibus paruis nocturna petunt Pabula ferœ: alius rupem
Himettus mons. Aphidnæ op.Dulcis Himetti, paruas alius Calcet Apidnas, pars illa diu Vacat immunis, qua curuati Littora ponti Sunion vrget.
main_text.head: Sunium promontorium, & vicus Atticæ.
main_text.p: Ovid. Meta. lib.6.Sunion expositum, Piraeaque tuta recessu Linquit, & in dextrum, qua iacet ora, latus. In freta deduci, veloque, & remige portus Cecropios intrat, Piraeaque litora tangit.
main_text.head: Eleusis vicus Atticæ.
main_text.p: Ovid. Fast. lib.4.Hadriacumque patens late, bimaremque Corinthum: Sic venit ad portus, Attica terra, tuos.
Triste saxum locus in Attica.Hic primum gelido sedit mœstissima saxo: Illud Cecropidæ nunc quoque triste vocant. Sub Ioue durauit multis immota diebus, Et luna patiens, & pluuialis aqua.
Fors sua cuique loco est, qui nunc Cerealis Eleusis Dicitur, hic Celeirura fuere senis.
Celeus ager in Attica.Ille domum glandes, excussaque mora rubetis Portat, & arsuris arida ligna focis.
Claud. de raptu Proserpinæ lib.1.Auditur fremitus terris, templumque remugit Cecropidum, sanctasque faces extollit Eleusis.

page.notes: Marginal references are partly worn; the Piræum note and the sign before "Attica terra" are uncertain. The verse at the top of the page is set in italic; the word "Hymet-" at the foot is a catchword fragment continuing onto the next page.
